additives.name: Disodium guanylate (627)
additives.what: Flavour enhancer that boosts savoury taste, usually used with MSG-type seasonings.
additives.note: Can be made from fish or meat — check the green dot if you are vegetarian/Jain.

additives.name: Disodium inosinate (631)
additives.what: Flavour enhancer that works with 627 to make snacks taste "moreish".
additives.note: Often animal-derived — check the green dot.

additives.name: Ribonucleotides (635)
additives.what: Mix of 627 + 631 flavour enhancers.

additives.name: Monosodium glutamate (621)
additives.what: Flavour enhancer (MSG). Safe in normal amounts but adds sodium.

additives.name: Maltodextrin
additives.what: Highly processed starch powder used to carry flavour. Raises blood sugar quickly.

additives.name: Hydrolysed vegetable protein
additives.what: Protein broken down to give a meaty/savoury taste. Sign of ultra-processing.

additives.name: Flavouring substances
additives.what: Added flavours (natural, nature-identical or artificial). Exact chemicals are not listed.

additives.name: Permitted colour
additives.what: Added colour to make the food look brighter. Not needed for nutrition.

additives.name: Caramel colour (150c/150d)
additives.what: Brown colour used in colas and malt drinks.

additives.name: Tartrazine (102)
additives.what: Yellow artificial colour. Linked to hyperactivity in some children.

additives.name: Sunset Yellow (110)
additives.what: Orange artificial colour. Linked to hyperactivity in some children.

additives.name: Acidity regulator (e.g. citric acid 330)
additives.what: Gives sourness and keeps flavour stable. Generally safe.

additives.name: Malic acid (296)
additives.what: Sour taste from fruit acid. Generally safe.

additives.name: Phosphoric acid (338)
additives.what: Acid in colas. Too much may affect teeth and bones.

additives.name: Anticaking agent (e.g. 551)
additives.what: Stops powders from clumping. Generally safe.

additives.name: Raising agents (500/501/503)
additives.what: Baking soda / ammonium bicarbonate to make biscuits light. Safe.

additives.name: Emulsifiers (322/442/476/471)
additives.what: Help oil and water mix. Common in chocolates and biscuits.

additives.name: Thickeners/stabilisers
additives.what: Make texture smooth or thick (guar gum 412, etc.).

additives.name: Preservative (e.g. sodium benzoate 211)
additives.what: Stops spoilage. Best limited, especially in drinks for kids.

additives.name: Antioxidant (Vitamin C, 300)
additives.what: Keeps colour and flavour fresh. Safe.

additives.name: Acetic acid (260)
additives.what: Vinegar acid. Safe.

additives.name: Palm oil / palmolein
additives.what: Cheap frying oil high in saturated fat.

additives.name: Caffeine
additives.what: Stimulant. Not recommended for children or in pregnancy in large amounts.

additives.name: Added sugar syrups
additives.codes: invert sugar, liquid glucose, dextrose, glucose syrup
additives.what: Hidden forms of sugar.

additives.name: Artificial sweetener
additives.what: Zero-calorie sweetener. Not advised for young children.

dishes.name: Veg thali
dishes.tips: A balanced plate: grains, dal for protein, sabzi and curd. | Go easy on the papad, pickle and extra ghee: that is where most of the salt and fat hide. | Make half the plate vegetables, as ICMR-NIN suggests.
dishes.swap: Extra papad and pickle -> A bowl of salad or kachumber

dishes.name: Pani puri
dishes.tips: The puris are deep-fried and the sweet chutney adds sugar. | Street pani can carry germs: pick a stall that uses filtered water. | Fine as an occasional treat, not a meal.
dishes.swap: Pani puri -> Sprouts chaat or a fruit chaat

dishes.name: Fresh fruit bowl
dishes.tips: Fruit sugar comes with fibre, so it does not count as "free sugar" in WHO advice. | Eat whole fruit rather than juice to keep the fibre. | Pick seasonal fruit: it is fresher, cheaper and tastier.
dishes.swap: Packaged fruit juice -> A whole fruit

dishes.name: Salted chips
dishes.tips: High in fat and salt for a small pack, with almost no protein or fibre. | Easy to overeat: the pack feels light but adds up fast. | Scan the packet to see its exact score.
dishes.swap: Salted potato chips -> Roasted chana or makhana

dishes.name: Plain dosa with sambar
dishes.tips: Fermented batter is easy to digest, and sambar adds dal and vegetables. | Ask for less oil or butter on the tawa. | Ragi or moong dosa adds even more fibre.
dishes.swap: Butter masala dosa -> Ragi or pesarattu dosa

dishes.name: Samosa
dishes.tips: Deep-fried maida pastry, so most of the energy comes from fat. | Reused frying oil at stalls can contain harmful trans fats. | Share one instead of having two.

dishes.name: Green salad
dishes.tips: Full of fibre, vitamins and water, with very few calories. | Add sprouts, paneer or chana to make it filling. | Keep creamy dressings light.
dishes.swap: Mayonnaise dressing -> Lemon, salt and chaat masala

dishes.name: Mithai (2 gulab jamun)
dishes.tips: Two pieces can pass the WHO ideal sugar limit for a whole day. | Fried and soaked in syrup: keep it for festivals. | One small piece is enough to enjoy the taste.
dishes.swap: Gulab jamun -> Fresh fruit chaat or dates

dishes.name: Vada pav
dishes.tips: A fried potato vada inside a maida pav: filling but low in protein. | The dry garlic chutney adds a lot of salt. | Pair it with buttermilk instead of a cold drink.
dishes.swap: Vada pav -> Methi thepla with curd

dishes.name: Cola
dishes.tips: About 9 teaspoons of sugar: more than the WHO ideal for a whole day. | Liquid sugar does not fill you up, so it is easy to overdo. | Kids should not have energy drinks or caffeine.
dishes.swap: Cola or soft drink -> Nimbu pani or coconut water
